title: Industrial policy events
note: Acts, programmes and institutions shaping Britain's energy and industrial trajectory. The mark is Royal Assent for an Act and the start date for a programme. Commencement, announcement and repeal stay separate. An overlapping Ready series is context, never an effect.

eras.label: Nationalisation
eras.focus: Public ownership of electricity supply and the post-war industrial settlement.

eras.label: Markets & regulation
eras.focus: Privatisation, licensing and the creation of independent energy regulators.

eras.label: Decarbonisation & strategy
eras.focus: Statutory carbon budgets, energy-system reform and modern industrial strategy.

events.title: Electricity Act 1947
events.summary: Established the British Electricity Authority and Area Electricity Boards, transferring electricity undertakers into public ownership. Royal Assent is printed as 13 August 1947. The Act (except specified savings) was later repealed by the Electricity Act 1989.
events.extent: Creates the British Electricity Authority and Area Boards for the supply of electricity in Great Britain, with related functions for the North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board. Northern Ireland is not treated as within the nationalisation scheme recorded here.

commencements.scope: legislation.gov.uk records the Act as wholly in force at Royal Assent.

events.status_note: Repealed by Electricity Act 1989 s.112(3)–(4) with savings; repeal in force 31 March 1990 by S.I. 1990/117. Recorded from legislation.gov.uk modifications text — not a causal claim about generation mix.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity generation by source
linked_indicators.note: National fuel mix is context for the public-ownership era — not an effect of the 1947 Act alone.

events.title: Electricity Act 1989
events.summary: Replaced the nationalised electricity boards with a licensing framework for generation, transmission and supply, and provided for vesting of Board assets in companies nominated by the Secretary of State. Royal Assent is printed as 27 July 1989.
events.extent: Core licensing and vesting provisions apply to England, Wales and Scotland. Later modifications transfer Director General functions to GEMA (Utilities Act 2000). Northern Ireland electricity law is not treated as identical here.

commencements.scope: First provisions in force (Director General, consumers' committees, interpretation). Further Parts followed by later orders.
Major vesting / licensing provisions and repeal of the 1947 Act (with savings).

events.status_note: Revised text remains on legislation.gov.uk. First commencement 1 September 1989 (S.I. 1989/1369); transfer/repeal wave 31 March 1990 (S.I. 1990/117). Later commencement orders exist — this seed pins the principal early dates, not every SI.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity generation by source
linked_indicators.note: Generation mix after privatisation is context — not proof the Act caused fuel substitution.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity interconnector flows
linked_indicators.note: Border flows sit in a later licensed market; link is contextual.

events.title: Utilities Act 2000
events.summary: Established the Gas and Electricity Markets Authority (Ofgem's statutory board) and the Gas and Electricity Consumer Council, and amended gas and electricity regulation. Royal Assent is printed as 28 July 2000.
events.extent: Creates GEMA and amends GB gas and electricity legislation. Consumer-body successors and later transfers are noted on legislation.gov.uk modifications; Northern Ireland regulators are separate.

commencements.citation: Utilities Act 2000 (Commencement No. 1 and Saving) Order 2000
commencements.scope: First appointed day for listed provisions (interpretation, savings powers, etc.). Sections 68 and 110 were already in force at Royal Assent.
Creation of GEMA and the Gas and Electricity Consumer Council (and related Schedules).

events.status_note: Key functions later transferred (e.g. consumer representation). Principal early commencements: 29 September 2000 (S.I. 2000/2412) and 1 November 2000 GEMA (S.I. 2000/2917). Further orders followed.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity interconnector flows
linked_indicators.note: Market regulation context for measured border flows — not an Ofgem decision log.

events.title: Climate Change Act 2008
events.summary: Set a 2050 greenhouse-gas reduction target, created a system of carbon budgets and established the Committee on Climate Change. Royal Assent is printed as 26 November 2008.
events.extent: United Kingdom. Section 95 defines national authorities as the Secretary of State, Scottish Ministers, Welsh Ministers and the relevant Northern Ireland department.

commencements.scope: Part 1 (carbon target and budgeting), Part 2 (Committee on Climate Change) and the commencement Part come into force on Royal Assent.
Other provisions (except those with special rules) come into force two months after Royal Assent.

events.status_note: Carbon-budget numbers and later target amendments are not copied into this seed. Commencement: Parts 1–2 on Royal Assent (26 November 2008); most remaining provisions on 26 January 2009 (s.100). Promise vs outcome needs commensurate official targets and series before scoring.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity generation by source
linked_indicators.note: Low-carbon share of generation is context for the Act's era — not a carbon-budget compliance score.

linked_indicators.title: Operational renewable planning sites
linked_indicators.note: REPD operational sites are a pipeline snapshot, not a statutory target outcome.

events.title: Energy Act 2023
events.summary: Wide energy-system statute covering carbon capture and storage licensing, hydrogen, the Independent System Operator and Planner, heat networks, energy-intensive industry support, offshore energy and civil nuclear provision. Royal Assent is printed as 26 October 2023.
events.extent: United Kingdom with Part-by-Part variation. See primary text and appointment regulations for remaining extents.

commencements.scope: Listed provisions come into force on Royal Assent (including this Part and specified hydrogen / system-operator / nuclear items). Not the whole Act.
Further listed Parts/Chapters come into force two months after Royal Assent. Remaining provisions commence by regulations.

events.status_note: Partially in force. Seed pins Royal-Assent wave (26 October 2023) and two-month wave (26 December 2023) from s.334; many other provisions commence by separate regulations — do not treat the whole Act as operative on assent.

linked_indicators.title: Electricity interconnector flows
linked_indicators.note: System-operator and market reforms are institutional context for measured border flows.

linked_indicators.title: Manufacturing employment
linked_indicators.note: Energy-intensive industry support language is not a measured jobs effect.

events.title: Modern Industrial Strategy 2025
events.summary: Ten-year cross-government industrial strategy published by the Department for Business and Trade, with sector plans including Clean Energy Industries. This record uses the GOV.UK collection published date as the programme start mark — it is not an Act and has no Royal Assent.
events.extent: United Kingdom strategy documents. Devolved delivery and funding routes differ by nation and are not enumerated here.
events.date_note: GOV.UK collection 'The UK's Modern Industrial Strategy 2025' published date (retrieved 2026-11-07). Not Royal Assent; sector plans have their own publication dates.
events.status_note: Strategy papers and sector plans are narrative evidence. Business-investment and manufacturing series linked below are context tracks only.

linked_indicators.title: Manufacturing output index
linked_indicators.note: Volume index is a production context track — not a scored strategy outcome.

linked_indicators.title: Manufacturing employment
linked_indicators.note: Workforce jobs are context for industrial strategy language — not proof of effect.

relationships.note: Electricity Act 1989 repealed the 1947 Act (with savings); SI 1990/117 brought the repeal into force on 31 March 1990.
Utilities Act 2000 amends electricity regulation and redirects Director General references to GEMA.
Energy Act 2023 inserts and amends provisions that interact with the Electricity Act 1989 licensing framework; commencement is by order.
